subject.title: Telegram agent: chatbot follow-up loop + exec tool aborts on pkill against earlier-spawned process

question: Should this combined report be split into the existing follow-up-policy tracker plus a narrow exec/process-control issue, or should maintainers define one coordinated invariant covering both Telegram reply behavior and raw shell process termination?
rationale: The source-backed gaps are real, but choosing how aggressively to mutate final replies and whether raw shell pkill should be supported versus steering to the managed process tool is product/process-boundary judgment.

options.title: Split And Scope First
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58450 for the follow-up policy half and keep or open a narrow process-control item for the raw pkill/session-kill behavior before implementation.

options.title: Keep One Coordinated Item
options.body: Treat both symptoms as one coordinated user-intent bug and require a maintainer-sponsored design plus live Telegram/Linux proof before any fix PR.

options.title: Support Managed Process Kill Only
options.body: Document and enforce that agents should use the process tool for earlier exec sessions, leaving arbitrary pkill shell behavior outside the supported contract unless a new repro proves otherwise.

recommendation.title: Split And Scope First
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58450 for the follow-up policy half and keep or open a narrow process-control item for the raw pkill/session-kill behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The broad follow-up-policy choice is the product-sensitive half and vignesh07 authored the closest current guard behavior.
